subject: physics
title: Forces and Exchange Particles
welcome_lead: Trade W, Z, gamma or gluon bosons to feel one of the four fundamental forces.
meta_desc: A-Level Particle Physics adventure on exchange particles and beta decay at quark level.
final_note: Beta decay is a down quark turning into an up by exchanging a W-minus.

concepts.def: Binds quarks; gluons exchange; short range.
W± and Z⁰ exchange; very short range.
d → u + W⁻ → u + e⁻ + ν̄_e.
u → d + W⁺ → d + e⁺ + ν_e.

walkthroughs.body_html: Each interaction is drawn with incoming particles, an exchange boson and outgoing particles. Time usually goes from left to right.
Inside a neutron, a down quark emits a W⁻, becoming an up quark — converting n to p. The W⁻ then decays into e⁻ + ν̄_e.
Strong: 10⁻¹⁵ m, very strong. EM: infinite range, 137× weaker. Weak: 10⁻¹⁸ m, ~10⁻⁶ relative. Gravity: infinite range but ~10⁻³⁹ relative.

mcqs.q: The exchange particle of the electromagnetic force is:
options: Gluon
W boson
Photon
Z boson
u becomes d, emits W⁺
d becomes u, emits W⁻
u becomes u, emits Z
d becomes s, emits gluon

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a fundamental particle: proton, electron, or neutron?
options: Mass changes with location but weight does not.
Only the electron — protons and neutrons are made of quarks.
Only the proton is fundamental; electrons and neutrons are composite.
All three (proton, electron, neutron) are fundamental particles that cannot be broken down.

mcqs.q: If an object is moving at constant velocity in a straight line, what is the net force on it?
options: The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
There must be a forward force on the object to keep it moving.
Zero — by Newton's first law, constant velocity requires zero net force.
Mass changes with location but weight does not.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
options: Mass changes with location but weight does not.
Mass is the amount of matter (kg); weight is the gravitational force on that mass (N) and depends on g.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
Mass and weight are the same thing, just expressed in different units.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Strong force”?
options: Binds quarks; gluons exchange; short range.
Photon exchange; infinite range.
Graviton (hypothetical); infinite range.
W± and Z⁰ exchange; very short range.
